newsitem.title: USA: US Congress inaction on shipbuilding disappointing.
newsitem.headline: US Congress inaction on shipbuilding disappointing.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Friday that she was disappointed by the failure of Congress to ratify an international agreement to eliminate government shipbuilding subsidies.

"Enactment of this legislation would have made it possible for American shipbuilders to compete on an equal footing with their foreign competitors," Barshefsky said in a statement. "Without the legislation, they will continue to be disadvantaged by huge foreign subsidies and predatory pricing practices the agreement sought to eliminate."

The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development shipbuilding agreement was signed by the United States in December 1994. Congress is expected to adjourn in the next few days without having voted on the legislation that would have implemented the pact.

The agreement would prohibit all subsidies to shipbuilders and establish a mechanism to address injurious pricing practices and address the way governments finance ship construction to avoid distortion of the market.
Barshefsky said the agreement would open international shipbuilding markets to U.S. shipyards.
